correctness.rationale: The exact Markov state (a,b,h) has intra-clique rates binom(a,2), binom(b,2), cross rate lambda h, and a hypergeometric loss in h after an internal dimer. On s=nt, the limiting vacant proportions and matched overlap are (1/(1+s),1/(1+s),1/(1+s)^2), yielding Poisson crossing intensity lambda/(1+s)^2. A bounded supermartingale Lyapunov F=h/a+h/b controls crossings after S/n by O(1/(1+S)), completing X_n=>Poisson(lambda). At jamming each clique has at most one vacancy; each cross-dimer removes one on either side, giving pathwise R_n=2 1_{n-X_n odd}, and the parity probabilities follow from the Poisson pgf. The proof's worst-case generator inequality was compared to the full earlier exact derivation and verifier state recurrences. The finite-state verifier code uses correct hypergeometric rates; no claim of having rerun its whole script is made.
